This is correct. The vast majority of enterprise workflows have not actually had agents applied to them in any meaningful way. The economy probably has this deployed < 1% right now.

At best you have a few automated systems in a company that do a single pass of an LLM to make a decision or provide feedback, but very little real “automation”. Some of this is a statement about the adoption rates of technology in enterprises, but the vast majority of it is really just due to the capability of AI itself.

That’s all changing. Now with computer use, long running agents, harness improvements and surrounding infrastructure, we’re finally at a point where we can start to apply agents at more complex workflows. 

We will see self-improving systems that can take any particular workflow goal and improve the execution rates over a volume of instances. And with the emerging form factor of agent swarms, you can just choose to deploy any amount of compute at a problem and agents will off and do the work.

This won’t be about and users prompting agents to complete a specific task for them, but instead the organization reengineering the underlying workflows to take advantage of agents in their processes. This will have a massive impact in finance, life sciences, healthcare, and other information-heavy domains. Lots of opportunity to build and deploy these systems right now.

Agents are going to consume 1,000X more tokens than we consume today. 

Because they’re going to be running in our workflows, processing all of our data, building out nearly all software, securing enterprises, and much more. To do this at scale we will need a variety of approaches at the frontier of AI. 

This includes continuing to push the boundaries of closed models, while also increasing the capability of open weights models, making them more secure, as well as making them more efficient for large workloads. 

Very exciting to see what @Suhail is building with Particle on this front.

Gemini 4 Carbon shifts the Pareto Frontier.

Where do users actually feel the difference with a frontier coding agent?

Across 20,869 Agent Arena traces, we compared how users criticized the five top models (all from @AnthropicAI & @OpenAI) on Agent Arena: Code, versus how they criticized other agents.

Here are 3 areas where frontier models make the most difference:

1. Less getting stuck: Among sessions with complaints, failed repair loops come up 6.9 percentage points less often, and project context gets ignored less often too (-1.9 pp). You spend less time steering the agent out of dead ends.

2. Better taste and code that works: They are better at design (-6.4 pp) and at producing working results (-5.8 pp). What you get back is more likely to be what you wanted.

3. More diligence: They follow instructions better (-5.6 pp), finish the work more often (-4.9 pp) and break existing work less (-4.5 pp). There's less to clean up afterwards.

Curious for a deeper dive into Agent Arena's praise vs complaint signal? See the article below in thread.

Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon is the new #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, and second only to Claude Opus 5.5 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index

Gemini 4 Carbon scores 59 on Intelligence Index v5, driven by leading performance in complex reasoning, knowledge, and scientific tasks. It also has large gains in coding and knowledge work, particularly when compared to other Gemini models, but it is not leading in all these areas.

As with launch of Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 4 Carbon is being rolled out to selected users and is not yet publicly available. Google is offering a 50% launch discount, with no confirmed end date. All our charts and figures use standard pricing for both Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon.

Key results for Gemini 4 Carbon with high reasoning:
➤ Gemini 4 Carbon leads the Intelligence Index v5, with the #1 score in 4 of the 9 Index evaluations: HLE-Diamond, Terminal-Bench-Science, AA-Omniscience, AutomationBench-AA. Carbon makes substantial gains elsewhere but is not leading in coding and knowledge work

➤ Behind only Claude Opus 5.5 on coding agents: With Antigravity CLI, Gemini 4 Carbon (high) scores 59 only 3 points behind Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 62) on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index. Carbon ranks second on both Terminal-Bench 4.0 (64%) and FrontierCode v1.1 (51%), behind Claude Opus 5.5 (max) at 56%. Google has historically underperformed in this area and so this improvement stands out

➤ Improved agentic knowledge work, but not yet leading: On AA-Briefcase, Gemini 4 Carbon (high) scores 1609 Elo, a 126-point improvement over Gemini 4 Argon (high, 1483), but still behind models including Grok 4.7 (xhigh, 1638), Muse Wonder (max, 1659) and Kimi K3.1 Pro (1678). The largest gain comes from Presentation, up 293 Elo to 1598, alongside a 120-point improvement in Analytical Quality to 1671

➤ Lower Cost per Task than Claude Opus 5.5 for comparable overall intelligence: Gemini 4 Carbon costs $7.76 per Intelligence Index task, ~23% less than Claude Opus 5.5 (max, $10.04) but ~1.2x GPT-6 Astra (max, $6.25). It uses 123k output tokens per task, 29% fewer than Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 173k). At the same $4/$20 standard pricing, its Cost per Task is in line with Gemini 4 Argon ($7.68), while scoring 9 points higher on the Intelligence Index

➤ Leading AA-Omniscience v1.1 score, with low hallucination: Gemini 4 Carbon scores 54 on our recently updated AA-Omniscience v1.1, 6 points ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 48) and 8 points ahead of Gemini 4 Argon (46). Accuracy (% correct) rises 10 points over Argon to 58%, while its hallucination rate rises from 4% to 11%. This is still the second lowest of any model, behind only Argon, compared with 50% for both Claude Opus 5.5 (max) and GPT-6 Astra (max)

Key model details:
➤ Context Window: 1M tokens
➤ Multimodality: Text, image, video, and speech input, with text output
➤ Pricing: $4/$20 per 1M input/output tokens, the same as Gemini 4 Argon’s standard pricing, with a 50% discount. Cached input tokens receive a 95% discount ($0.20 per 1M)

AssemblyAI has launched its first Text to Speech model! AssemblyAI-TTS-1 enters the top 12 in our Provider Voice Arena and the top 10 in Controlled Voice

@AssemblyAI has launched its first Text to Speech model, AssemblyAI-TTS-1! We evaluated its performance across both Speech Arenas and our Pronunciation Robustness benchmark.

Key takeaways:

➤ Text to Speech, Provider Voice: AssemblyAI-TTS-1 scores an Elo of 1,227 across 1,626 arena appearances, ranking #12, just behind Breeze TTS 2 at 1,228 and ahead of Mistral's Voxtral 3 TTS at 1,221 and Inworld's Realtime TTS-2 Flash at 1,218. It ranks #12 in both English (US) and English (UK).

➤ Text to Speech, Controlled Voice: AssemblyAI-TTS-1 scores 1,110 across 1,674 appearances, ranking #10 with the same 8 cloned voices, behind Cartesia's Sonic 3.5 at 1,118 and ahead of Speechify's Simba 3.2 at 1,086. It ranks #6 in Knowledge Sharing.

➤ Pronunciation Robustness: AssemblyAI-TTS-1 scores 81.7% across 2,115 rated clips, ranking #16, behind HeyGen Voice at 83.2% and ahead of Inworld Realtime TTS-2 at 80.7%. It ranks #6 in Preserving Exact Sequences at 81.5%.

➤ Speed: AssemblyAI-TTS-1 generates 162 characters per second, faster than Cartesia's Sonic 3.6 at 148.6 and Mistral's Voxtral 3 TTS at 112.3.

➤ Pricing: AssemblyAI-TTS-1 is priced at $15/1M characters. Of the eleven models ranked above it on Provider Voice, only two cost less: Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS at $11/1M and Simba 3.2 at $6.6/1M. Eleven v4 is $80/1M and Sonic 3.6 $49/1M.

Vercel CI solves the "AI coding bottleneck" via:
① Fast and stable infrastructure (faster work)
② Turborepo integration (less work)
③ Agentic CI

① is obvious. Your CI is slow, flaky, goes down. We solve that. We operate 20 worldwide clusters doing millions of microVMs per day.

② is less obvious, but very powerful. Turborepo was designed to intelligently skip and cache prior work. The graph of dependencies is computed, not written. 

Ask your agent to migrate to @turborepo and start saving money and time. Even if you don't use us. But you should, it's really good.

③ is a game-changer. 𝚟𝚎𝚛𝚌𝚎𝚕 𝚌𝚒 in the CLI is the first step, because now your agents can inspect, abort, trigger, replay CI. Vercel Agent can help optimize it. And this is just the start.

You can expect a lot of hooks and capabilities to make CI something far more intelligent, that can even capture the nuance and judgment an engineer would have ("Are those tests even worth running?")

Agentic CI is the future of how we ship software. Excited to build it with you all!

You build a habitat where they can do great work, with boundaries that contain the damage when things go wrong.
